subject.title: feat: keep reset session history searchable

question: Should explicit `/reset` and `/new` retain prior SQLite generations as searchable history by default, with only explicit deletion or physical disk pressure reclaiming them?
rationale: This is a deliberate user-visible retention-policy and storage-lifecycle change, not merely a mechanical bug repair; the protected maintainer label also requires explicit human handling.

options.title: Sponsor durable reset history
options.body: Accept searchable historical generations as the reset default, contingent on upgrade and real-runtime proof for reset, delete, and pressure paths.

options.title: Keep archive-and-remove resets
options.body: Retain the existing reset lifecycle and limit any preservation work to a separately approved, opt-in retention design.

options.title: Narrow the proposal
options.body: Keep the reset-retention direction but defer physical pressure eviction until its policy and upgrade behavior are reviewed separately.

recommendation.title: Sponsor durable reset history
recommendation.body: Accept searchable historical generations as the reset default, contingent on upgrade and real-runtime proof for reset, delete, and pressure paths.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the merged reset-policy work and the current implementation, making them the best available routing candidate for the intended session-retention direction.
